content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Ashley Roberts (E016) requests write access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- HR note: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommends write for Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write, admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist does), so write is fine. Recommend write.
- Security note: role Analyst (not looked up), employment type contractor, security training basic. Security DB authoritative for employment type/training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training means max read. Recommend read.

The two notes conflict. HR says full_time, Security says contractor with basic training. Security DB is authoritative for employment type/training per note 2.

Access policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → max read.

Requested write > max read → grant max = read.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Security DB is authoritative for employment type; lists contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write with advanced training. Basic training limits to read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.
